issue.title: Rendering of reference and pointer parameters in markdown script
issue.body:
Currently a parameter with a ref or pointer renders with a space after the ref like this: `Device & somedevice` or `Device * somedevice` (rendering is fine value parameters).

The question is, should this render as `Device& somedevice` or `Device &somedevice`

(as an aside, the second format is slightly harder, because for pointers, care needs to be taken to make sure the * is not interpreted as "make text italic".

This originates here: https://github.com/dronecore/docs/pull/107#discussion_r174682278

comments.body: Which is best is a matter of style - have we standardized on this in source code?

> But `Device & somedevice` is hard to read. Isn't it ?

IMO it is easy to read, but it looks a little unnatural. I have fixed this in https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/pull/324

It uses `Device& somedevice` for parameters. This is easier to implement and looks better in more cases.

FYI, the prototypes etc are still rendered with odd spaces. It would be a lot more effort to tidy these cases up because the whole strings are provided by doxygen.

This has been set with #410 in:

https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/blob/develop/.clang-format#L55 

to `Device &somedevice`.

There are [pros and cons](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/398395/why-is-the-asterisk-before-the-variable-name-rather-than-after-the-type), however, the [CppCoreGuidelines](https://github.com/isocpp/CppCoreGuidelines/blob/master/CppCoreGuidelines.md#nl18-use-c-style-declarator-layout ) suggest to use `Device& somedevice`.

Given that I would suggest we switch it. It's as easy as changing `.clang-format` and doing `make fix_style`.

@julianoes In above, `Device &somedevice` = `Device &somedevice` :-)

Whatever alignment is used is fine as long as we're consistent.

➤ Hamish Willee commented:

Julian Oes Long time since this discussion... and I thought it was "done". Can you remind me what action, if any, I am supposed to take here?
We should change it to `Device& somedevice` according to [CppCoreGuidelines](https://github.com/isocpp/CppCoreGuidelines/blob/master/CppCoreGuidelines.md#nl18-use-c-style-declarator-layout).
I can do the change after the rename.

Cool. So when the code is all "right" I'll have another look and see if I can match it in markdown. Note though, that this sort of thing is fiddly, and as long as the code is readable in markdown I do not see this as my highest priority.

issue.title: Function parameter reference/pointer types fix

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Addresses https://github.com/dronecore/DroneCore/issues/321. Basically a function parameter type for a reference or pointer will now render with the * or & immediately next to the type.
```
#old
Device * somedevice
Device & somedevice
#new
Device* somedevice
Device& somedevice
```
IFF the type is a pointer, then the "*" is escaped (so markdown doesn't think we want to change case to italic).

Note, I decided on aligning symbol to type rather than name, because this works better in more cases.

issue.title: Change clang-format style

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
**AlignAfterOpenBracket -> AlwaysBreak**

The main reason for this change is to work around a clang-format bug in AlignAfterOpenBracked introduced with clang-format 8:
https://bugs.llvm.org/show_bug.cgi?id=41676

By changing to this option, we resolve the problem were different versions enforce different styles.

Also, in my opinion this style makes more sense in general.
For some argumentation by Kevlin Henney, I suggest to watch:
https://youtu.be/ZsHMHukIlJY?t=1027


**PointerAlignment -> Left**

We wanted to switch the pointer and reference alignment style for a while. Given now we just had many automatic changes with the previous style change as well as the rename, it makes sense to do this change
now.

The reasoning is mostly that this is more common in C++ in general and that it is recommended by the CppCoreGuidelines.
https://github.com/isocpp/CppCoreGuidelines/blob/master/CppCoreGuidelines.md#nl18-use-c-style-declarator-layout

Closes #412 and fixes #321.
